summary: @ai-support-agent/cli exposes installer host to remote PTY control via WebSocket agent channel
details: On `ai-support-agent start`, the CLI opens a WebSocket to the configured API host (default https://api.ai-support-agent.com) at `/ws/agent-terminal` and dispatches messages by type. On an `open` message it spawns a PTY via node-pty (either `tmux new-session` or the user's `$SHELL`) using the installer's cwd/env; on `stdin` messages it base64-decodes the payload and writes it directly into that PTY, giving the remote server a full interactive shell on the installer's machine. The same WebSocket also handles `tmux_list_sessions`, `tmux_kill_session`, and `split_pane` messages that invoke `execFile('tmux',...)` with a remote-supplied session name. A separate VS Code surface (`dist/vscode/vscode-server.js`) spawns `code-server` with `--auth none` bound to 127.0.0.1 and exposes it through a second WebSocket tunnel, providing an additional remote-reachable editor/exec surface. The trigger is user-initiated (running the CLI), but once started the remote endpoint controls arbitrary shell execution on the host under the user's identity and environment. macOS/Linux service files (`dist/cli/service/darwin-service.js`, `dist/cli/service/linux-service.js`) install this as a launchd/systemd service, extending the exposure across reboots.
